stem: Two containers receive the same irrigation volume, but one dries much faster between events after the crop has grown larger. What is the best interpretation?
choices: Dryback reflects changing plant demand as well as media and root development, so irrigation timing may need adjustment
The equal irrigation volume suggests dryback should remain similar, so the faster change is most likely a sensor-placement artifact
Container color is a likely primary explanation because surface heating generally controls most root-zone moisture loss between irrigation events
Larger plants can change canopy demand, but root-zone depletion should remain stable if the irrigation volume and medium are unchanged
rationale: Dryback is a change in root-zone moisture over time and can shift as plant demand, root development, media behavior, and environmental conditions change.
